sources.title: Swiss Ephemeris Programming Interface
sources.author: Astrodienst
sources.verified_scope: Official documentation was inspected for Julian-calendar conversion, astronomical year numbering, UT versus ET/TT handling, Delta-T, ephemeris selection, return flags, named sidereal modes, and file coverage. The official seplm06.se1 and semom06.se1 files covering 601 BCE through 2 BCE were acquired from the Swiss Ephemeris repository, byte-counted, SHA-256 hashed, and used with library 2.10.03 for all 192 Rochberg Texts 2-27 published-position reproductions. sources.title: NASA/JPL Horizons System and API
sources.author: NASA/JPL Solar System Dynamics
sources.verified_scope: The official API documentation and Horizons manual were inspected for geocentric observer location 500@399, TDB/UT handling, ancient target coverage, and output quantities 30 and 31. API version 1.2 was queried for all 192 Rochberg table positions. For the first 67, same-UT differences peak at 0.0306521 degrees overall and 0.0031827 degrees for non-lunar bodies, Horizons-minus-Swiss Delta-T is 95.059-224.735 seconds, and all same-TT differences are at most 0.0008223 degrees. For the 125-position Texts 11-27 extension, same-UT differences peak at 0.0148495 degrees overall and 0.001646 degrees for non-lunar bodies, Horizons-minus-Swiss Delta-T ranges from -41.945 to 90.342 seconds, and all same-TT differences are at most 0.0008398 degrees. Mars, Jupiter, and Saturn barycenters (targets 4, 5, and 6) were required because the corresponding planet-center trajectories do not cover these ancient dates; that limitation is preserved in both validation specifications.
sources.rights_note: Review NASA/JPL attribution, service, and data-use terms before commercial caching or redistribution. A successful public API query is not itself a commercial-rights determination.
sources.next_action: Freeze response provenance or reproduce the comparison from an independently versioned offline JPL SPK pipeline, review attribution and caching terms, and set prospective tolerances before promoting any result to a golden oracle.

sources.title: Babylonian Horoscopes
sources.author: Francesca Rochberg
sources.repository: Ancient World Digital Library, NYU Institute for the Study of the Ancient World; permission from American Philosophical Society
sources.verified_scope: The 184-page searchable edition scan was acquired and hash-verified. The complete catalogue and every passage in Texts 1-32 were inspected in transcription, translation, apparatus, commentary, tables, and rendered page images. The edition has 31 catalogued horoscope entries across 28 numbered horoscope texts; Text 11 explicitly duplicates Text 10, leaving 30 catalogued entries after that collapse, but Text 28 may originally have contained more than one horoscope, so this is not a unique-nativity count. Four birth-note tablets preserve six births, including three distinct notices in Text 32. Texts 1-10 contain sixteen judgment clauses, Text 16 adds three damaged or uncertain candidates, and Text 27 adds two upper-edge fortune fragments with no recoverable protasis; none is customer-executable. All 192 published longitude targets from Texts 2-27 were independently recomputed with a locked Swiss Ephemeris DE431/Moshier profile and cross-checked against NASA/JPL Horizons at both the same UT labels and the same TT instants. The 125-position extension preserves thirteen exploratory Rochberg-table tolerance failures, including a 2.1036-degree Text 18 Saturn residual and a strong Text 23 one-day table-label conflict; its independent Horizons same-TT comparison nevertheless agrees within 0.0008398 degrees, showing that those edition-table conflicts are not ephemeris implementation failures. Text 1 was separately reconstructed as twelve surrounding events rather than a natal chart. Event-year and Seleucid-year layers, damage, restorations, record-boundary uncertainty, computation assumptions, KI qaqqaru, visibility criteria, and uncertain birth times remain explicit.
sources.rights_note: AWDL provides the copyrighted scan for noncommercial research and educational use with APS permission; commercial reuse beyond fair use requires permission.
sources.next_action: Freeze the Horizons response provenance or reproduce it through an offline JPL SPK pipeline; resolve the two remaining institutional object joins for W 20030/143 and W 20030/10 and perform image-level collation; reconstruct calendar and delta-T uncertainty intervals; implement visibility models only after their observational criteria are established; resolve lunar-latitude and KI/house-scheme hypotheses under named packs; obtain Assyriological review; and acquire commercial permission or a separately licensed basis before publication.

sources.author: Sebastian Porceddu and coauthors
sources.repository: Cambridge Archaeological Journal; author-hosted PDF inspected

It enumerates nine full or partial hemerological sources, documents twelve 30-day months in three four-month seasons plus five heriu-renpet days, reports no prognosis data for the five final days in its compared corpus, and analyzes Cairo 86637, BM 10474 and Sallier IV. Budge 1923 independently shows that Sallier IV's likely epagomenal portion is lost, so the paper's missing final-day data must not be generalized into historical nonexistence. Its periodicity and within-day timing models are modern statistical interpretations, not ancient executable rules.
sources.rights_note: Use as a scholarly analysis under publisher/author terms; do not reproduce the article.

sources.verified_scope: The page identifies Thai and Lanna inscriptional evidence containing chart and Suriyayatra-derived quantities, including a Chiang Mai foundation record reconstructed to 12 April 1296 Julian, and distinguishes 27 stellar groups and historical calendrical practice.
sources.rights_note: Government-page reuse terms and underlying inscription rights require review.
sources.next_action: Trace every named inscription to its edition and image; use them as blind historical calculation fixtures rather than accepting the interview's conversions uncritically.

sources.title: Thai Astrology and Suriyayatra Study Curricula
sources.author: Foundation of the Astrological Association of Thailand under ecclesiastical patronage
sources.verified_scope: The current curricula enumerate separate calculation and judgment domains including astronomy, zodiac, ascendant construction, natal and transit charts, Thaksa, Tri-Wai, planetary age periods, Suriyayatra, Manat and military-electional charting.
sources.rights_note: Current curriculum content is not a primary historical rule authority and may change.
sources.next_action: Engage the institution for school/convention mapping, complete worked charts, terminology review, and living-practice validation.

sources.title: The Burmese and Arakanese Calendars
sources.author: A. M. B. Irwin
sources.repository: Public-domain scan digitized by Internet Archive
sources.verified_scope: The monograph and OCR were inspected for source identity, corrections, Burmese/Arakanese distinctions, intercalary months/days, historical official practice, Thandeikta changes, conversion tables, and the author's proposed reforms. It acknowledges named Mandalay and Kemmendine informants and also contains colonial-era assumptions that require review.
sources.rights_note: 1909 scan is public domain; verify Wikimedia/Internet Archive attribution and keep modern annotations separate.
sources.next_action: Transcribe exact algorithms with corrigenda, separate observed historical tables from Irwin's reforms, and compare against indigenous Thandeikta/Makaranta texts and modern official calendars.

sources.title: Parabaik: Handbook for Astrological Works, MAP 19777
sources.author: Possibly associated with U Ottara; uncertain
sources.repository: Asia and Pacific Museum in Warsaw
sources.verified_scope: The museum identifies a 1925 Burmese/Pali/Pa'O paper manuscript containing formulas, constellation/year illustrations beginning with birth statements, and calculation diagrams, alongside magical, protection and healing content. The attribution/date relationship is uncertain.
sources.rights_note: The catalog states public domain; confirm download-image attribution and API terms.
sources.next_action: Download all folios, order recto/verso sequences, obtain Burmese/Pali/Pa'O transcription, and separate natal calculations from ritual or medical material.

sources.title: Astrology in Burmese Buddhist Culture: Decoding an Illustrated Manuscript from the SOAS Archives
sources.author: Elizabeth Moore
sources.verified_scope: The repository abstract identifies a late-nineteenth/early-twentieth-century illustrated SOAS manuscript and states that the article explains basic principles of Burmese astrology while decoding its broader Buddhist, court and cosmological imagery.
sources.rights_note: The article is copyrighted and full text was not available from the inspected repository page.
sources.next_action: Acquire the article and manuscript shelfmark/images; do not treat the abstract's general principles as executable rules.

sources.title: Astronomie cambodgienne
sources.author: Felix Gaspard Faraut
sources.repository: Gallica / Musee du quai Branly-Jacques Chirac
sources.edition: Phnom Penh and Saigon, 1910, 283 pages plus plate
sources.verified_scope: Institutional/bibliographic metadata and the modern technical study identify the work as the detailed source for Khmer astronomer-astrologer integer recipes. A direct Gallica PDF request returned HTTP 429, so the scan itself was not inspected in this pass.
sources.rights_note: Gallica states commercial reuse of its digitization requires a license; underlying 1910 text is public domain in relevant jurisdictions subject to verification.
sources.next_action: Acquire through Gallica or a partner library, hash the scan, inspect Faraut's local informants and terminology, and collate all tables against Vernotte/Kichenassamy.

sources.title: Astronomie et astrologie cambodgienne, FR EFEO P.CAMB/Paris/160
sources.verified_scope: The archival record lists 120 partially numbered folios of Cambodian astronomy, seven folios plus a foldout of astronomy/astrology, thirteen folios for EF manuscript 106 Pheisantar, a French translation of a palm-leaf divination collection, and Sun/Moon notes.
sources.rights_note: Access and reproduction conditions are not stated on the record and must be negotiated with EFEO.
sources.next_action: Request the complete file and original EF 106 witness, establish dates/provenance, and align the French translation to Khmer/Pali source folios.

sources.title: Influences of Thai Divination on Cambodian Fortune-Telling Practice
sources.author: Poonnatree Jiaviriyaboonya
sources.verified_scope: The article documents birth-date numerology, old-scripture, royal, market and other practices in Phnom Penh; the loss and restricted transmission of Khmer manuals; and extensive reliance on named Thai books by contemporary practitioners. It explicitly reports no single standardized contemporary Cambodian technique.
sources.rights_note: Publisher copyright applies; field interlocutor identities and consent context must be respected.
sources.next_action: Use this as a transmission and living-practice map, not a rulebook; partner with Khmer scholars/practitioners and distinguish inherited Khmer, Thai-derived and individual hybrid methods.

sources.title: Daivajnakamadhenu
sources.author: Anomadassi Sangharaja Mahasthavira; edited by C. A. Seelakkhandha Sthavira and Seetarama Upadhyaya
sources.verified_scope: The 1905 Chaukhamba/Benares Sanskrit Series edition is 318 pages. Its title matter identifies the work with Anomadassi of Hastavanagalya Parivena in Ceylon and the editors in Ceylon and Benares. The 434945-byte romanized OCR (SHA-256 017833cb89b7eda054003c9da3a0375ee9921a6756824b59f53100e9ead8355c) and scan contents expose thirty chapters and 198 indexed sections covering astronomy and calendrics, natal judgment, longevity, planetary periods, ashtakavarga, combinations, interrogation, elections, compatibility, omens, travel, agriculture and ritual/medical material.
sources.rights_note: Historical scan access is public through the repository; confirm reuse terms before storing or redistributing page images or OCR. Customer-facing rules require scan verification and a licensed or independently produced translation.
sources.next_action: Create a folio/page concordance, verify OCR passages against the scan and a second edition, identify cited source strata, and have Sanskrit and Sinhala-domain reviewers classify which procedures belong to historical Sri Lankan practice.

sources.title: Conceptualising the World in Pali Literature
sources.author: Alastair Gornall
sources.repository: Journal of the Pali Text Society / Heidelberg Asian Studies Publishing
sources.verified_scope: The study identifies Anomadassi as a thirteenth-century Mahavihara monk in Sri Lanka and the author of an early Sanskrit astronomical anthology, while separately tracing Pali astral and cosmological works in Myanmar, including the Candasuriyagatidipani and its mixed Pali, Sanskrit jyotisa and canonical source environment. It supports transmission history and source discovery, not atomic divinatory rules.
sources.rights_note: Publisher copyright applies; cite and paraphrase within scholarly-use limits.
sources.next_action: Follow the article's manuscript and edition references, then verify every proposed calculation or judgment in the cited primary witness rather than importing the article's historical synthesis as a rule.

sources.title: Sinhalese Astrology, South Asian Caste Systems, and the Notion of Individuality
sources.author: Steven E. G. Kemper
sources.repository: The Journal of Asian Studies / Cambridge University Press
sources.verified_scope: The article and its accessible notes document person-specific Sinhalese horoscopy, counterclockwise chart layout, the importance of the birth nakat, and a locally described use of the eight-category, thirty-six-point marriage comparison. It is evidence for practice boundaries and terminology, not a complete calculation manual.
sources.rights_note: Publisher copyright applies; full article access and quotation limits must be respected.
sources.next_action: Acquire the full article and its cited Sinhala sources, obtain worked chart and matching examples from qualified practitioners, and test whether thresholds and scoring categories vary by school or period.

sources.title: Palm Leaf Manuscript Reading Service
sources.author: University of Sri Jayewardenepura Library
sources.verified_scope: The university describes a palm-leaf collection containing astrology among other subjects, in Pali, Sinhala and Sanskrit, predominantly from the eighteenth and nineteenth centuries, with supervised onsite reading access.
sources.rights_note: Access is permission-based and may require fees; manuscript photography, transcription and publication rights must be negotiated item by item.
sources.next_action: Request the astrology shelf list and descriptive catalog, prioritize dated procedural witnesses and almanacs, and commission language-specific cataloging before selecting implementation sources.

sources.title: University of Peradeniya Sanskrit astrology curriculum
sources.author: Department of Classical Languages, University of Peradeniya
sources.verified_scope: The curriculum identifies horoscope construction, auspicious times, planetary periods, signs, planets, Moon and stars, and prescribes selected Brhajjataka chapters; related university course documents also identify Panchanga, Shadvarga, naming and marriage matching as taught in Sri Lankan social context.
sources.rights_note: Public institutional curriculum; linked course materials remain subject to university copyright.
sources.next_action: Use the bibliography to acquire the exact editions and Sinhala teaching texts, and recruit instructors to supply calculation conventions and worked examples.

sources.title: BAMS curriculum: Principles of Astrology
sources.author: Institute of Indigenous Medicine, University of Colombo
sources.verified_scope: The curriculum lists zodiac, Panchanga, Bhavakaraka, horoscope preparation and prediction, and names Sinhala reference works including Lagna Chandrikava and Nakshatra Nighantuva. The curriculum is a bibliography and scope map, not a rule authority.
sources.rights_note: University copyright applies; obtain and license or independently translate the named books before deriving rules.
sources.next_action: Locate the exact cited Sinhala editions, record publication and lineage metadata, and obtain bilingual technical review before encoding any procedure.

sources.title: 2026 New Year auspicious-times announcement
sources.author: Department of Cultural Affairs, Sri Lanka
sources.verified_scope: The official announcement records a state process in which astrologers and almanac writers reach consensus on New Year auspicious times. It confirms living institutional practice but does not publish a reproducible calculation kernel.
sources.rights_note: Government webpage; verify terms before reuse and preserve the announcement date because annual values change.
sources.next_action: Acquire the official almanac and committee calculation record for multiple years, then compare the stated instants with candidate solar-ingress and electional procedures.

sources.title: Sri Lankan Tamil Palm-Leaf Manuscripts: astrology records
sources.verified_scope: The catalog search exposes Sri Lankan Tamil palm-leaf records explicitly classified under astrology, including titles associated with jataka and astronomical/astrological sciences. This is a distinct Tamil-language research track and is not evidence for Sinhala rules.
sources.rights_note: Catalog metadata is public; image, transcription and reuse conditions are item-specific.
sources.next_action: Open each item record, identify language, script, date, completeness and image access, then select a procedural witness with Tamil scholarly review.

sources.title: Recalling a Translocal Past: Digitizing Mon Palm-Leaf Manuscripts of Thailand
sources.author: Southeast Asia Junction; EAP1432 project team
sources.repository: SEA Junction / British Library Endangered Archives Programme
sources.verified_scope: The project description reports nearly one thousand manuscripts, mostly nineteenth to early twentieth century, in Mon and Pali using Mon script alongside Thai and Pali in Khom script, with astrology and divination among the represented subjects. It establishes a corpus but not a specific birth-reading procedure.
sources.rights_note: EAP and holding-monastery access and reuse conditions apply; community provenance and custodial permissions must be retained.
sources.next_action: Obtain the complete EAP1432 catalog export, classify language separately from script and genre, and identify one complete Mon-language procedural astrology manuscript for community-reviewed transcription.

sources.title: EAP1432 Methodology Report
sources.author: EAP1432 project team
sources.verified_scope: Indexed metadata indicates that secular materials including horoscopology were prioritized and that language expertise and catalog accuracy are material limitations. The report itself was not successfully retrieved in this pass, so none of its details are promoted to rule evidence.
sources.rights_note: British Library/EAP terms apply; retrieve the report before quoting or relying on its methodological claims.
sources.next_action: Acquire and inspect the report, record its cataloging limitations precisely, and require Mon-language community correction before treating catalog labels as authoritative.

sources.title: U Po Thi Library manuscript catalog
sources.author: Myanmar Manuscript Digital Library
sources.verified_scope: The Thaton collection includes astrology and several explicitly astral titles, including works on intercalation, longevity/periods, solar-lunar motion, zodiacal signs and nakshatras. The inspected records do not establish that those titles are Mon-language: Mon State provenance, Myanmar script, Pali content and Mon ethnic attribution must not be conflated.
sources.rights_note: Catalog and manuscript-image terms are repository-specific; local custodial rights and attribution must be preserved.
sources.next_action: Inspect item-level language, script and colophon metadata for the astral titles, request images where available, and promote no item to the Mon rule corpus without linguistic confirmation.

sources.title: George Coedes' Chronology of the Kingdom of Haripunjaya
sources.verified_scope: The direct endpoint returned an HTML analytics shell rather than the indexed article or a PDF. No technical claim from search snippets has been accepted as evidence.
sources.rights_note: Unknown until the actual article and publication record are obtained.
sources.next_action: Locate the article through the journal or a library, then assess its critique of the proposed Haripunjaya calendar and local intercalation against epigraphic primary evidence.

sources.title: Book of Nativities and Book of Revolution
sources.author: Abraham Ibn Ezra
sources.verified_scope: Repository provenance records parallel Hebrew-English critical text inspection, SHA-256, precise rules and edition limitations.
sources.rights_note: Copyrighted Brill edition; internal verification only and no redistribution.
sources.next_action: Define an Ibn Ezra-specific pack and inventory the rest of his astrological corpus without conflating Arabic source traditions.

sources.title: Anwa and lunar-station primary source audit
sources.repository: ISMI, OCIANA, University of Arizona, and scholarly edition catalogs
sources.verified_scope: The Ibn Qutayba edition and four-witness manuscript path, direct Ancient North Arabian inscription corpora, and major source-critical scholarship are now mapped. The evidence does not establish a pre-Islamic natal reading, and the later uniform twenty-eight-station framework may reorganize earlier rain-star complexes.
sources.rights_note: Rights differ across public-domain manuscripts, corpus images, copyrighted scholarship and modern editions; every acquired item needs its own record.
sources.next_action: Acquire Ibn Qutayba's Arabic witnesses and edition, the Varisco article and Adams dissertation; build poetry, inscription, philological and later-system layers; then test star identifications and horizon phenomena without imposing equal sectors.

sources.title: Manual of Mongolian Astrology and Divination
sources.author: Antoine Mostaert; edited by Francis Woodman Cleaves
sources.repository: Harvard University Press / library catalog records
sources.verified_scope: The inspected Google Books and library records identify a 127-page 1969 Scripta Mongolica volume devoted to a Mongolian astrology/divination manual and expose a limited terminology index. The book's text and source-manuscript description were not inspected, so no rule is verified.
sources.rights_note: Harvard University Press copyright applies; acquire a lawful copy for internal analysis and do not redistribute text or scans.
sources.next_action: Acquire the complete volume, identify the underlying Mongolian witness and edition method, and create a passage-level inventory of calculations, inputs, judgments and variants.

sources.title: Shira jiruqai-yin yosun bui: chagh ularil-un toghan-u ujelge
sources.repository: Ernst Collection catalogue, Bern Open Publishing
sources.verified_scope: Catalogue item 139 identifies Mongolian manuscript GDC Mong M2:3 / ET_875, fifteen folios plus three additional folios, with diagrams and Mongolian pagination. The cataloger classifies it as an astrological-divinatory manual of favorable and unfavorable days for activities in the four seasons and supplies incipit and explicit transcriptions.
sources.rights_note: The 2025 catalogue is CC BY 4.0; manuscript-image rights and access are separate.
sources.next_action: Request complete manuscript images, transcribe the Mongolian text, align activities and day conditions by folio, and locate a parallel witness or practitioner example.

sources.title: Manual of Astrology and Divination
sources.verified_scope: Indexed NLM curatorial metadata describes a nineteenth-century manuscript from Mongolia, written in Tibetan, with calculation diagrams for planetary motion, eclipses and auspicious activities. Direct page access returned HTTP 429 in this pass. Mongolian provenance must not be confused with Mongolian language or a uniquely Mongolian rule set.
sources.rights_note: NLM image and manuscript terms require inspection; health-related content must remain Historical Use Only and cannot become medical advice.
sources.next_action: Obtain the NLM item identifier, images and curator metadata through the library, then have Tibetan and Mongolian specialists identify the textual source and local adaptations.

sources.title: Yuriy Nurdaev, About Mongolian astrology
sources.author: Baasanjav Terbish; Yuriy Nurdaev
sources.repository: University of Cambridge Kalmyk Cultural Heritage Documentation Project
sources.verified_scope: The repository abstract records Kalmyk uses of Mongolian astrology for choosing days for rituals, holidays, construction, weddings, funerals and hunting, and for weather forecasting, while noting Chinese and Tibetan influence. The 8.68 GB interview was not viewed and the record provides no calculation procedure.
sources.rights_note: CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 applies except where otherwise noted; respect the interviewee, community context and noncommercial/no-derivatives restrictions.
sources.next_action: View and index the interview within license terms, recruit Kalmyk community review, and keep Kalmyk practice distinct from Mongolian state and Inner Mongolian lineages.

sources.title: Types and Characteristics of the 18th Century Mongolian Astronomy
sources.repository: Dankook University Institute of Mongolian Studies / Kyobo Scholar
sources.verified_scope: The accessible abstract treats zurkhai as astronomical, astrological and calendrical knowledge, describes Chinese and Tibetan/Indian transmission and Mongolian adaptation, and identifies the eighteenth century as a period of regional systematization. It names Merged garakhin oron as a focal work but supplies no reproducible formula in the accessible page.
sources.rights_note: Publisher copyright applies; full article access is required for detailed use.
sources.next_action: Acquire the complete article, resolve author/title transliterations, follow its primary bibliography and map distinct regional calendar systems.

sources.title: Mongolian Ancient Works
sources.author: Inner Mongolia University Library
sources.verified_scope: The university catalog reports 13115 ancient works, supports Mongolian, Chinese and Latin-script title searching, and makes selected items available online. No astrology item was promoted from the unfiltered landing page.
sources.rights_note: Catalog and item rights are repository-specific; contact Inner Mongolia University Library for reuse.
sources.next_action: Search in Mongolian script and transliteration for zurkhai, calendar, divination and named authors, then verify language, edition, completeness and access item by item.

sources.title: A Study on the Process of the Inflow of Saju-myeongri prior to the Early Joseon
sources.author: Kim Mantae
sources.repository: Kyujanggak Institute for Korean Studies / Korea Citation Index
sources.verified_scope: The accessible abstract traces early forms and the later Ziping system into Korea, identifies Ohaengchonggwal as a 1458 Korean work, and records Japyeongsammyeongtongbyeonyeonwon as a Joseon Myeonggwahak textbook. It supports lineage boundaries and primary-source routing, not atomic judgment rules.
sources.rights_note: Publisher copyright applies; full text and quotation terms must be obtained before passage-level use.
sources.next_action: Acquire the full paper, inspect its primary citations, and build a Korean-to-Chinese witness concordance that distinguishes adoption, local commentary and later practice.

sources.title: A Study on Seo Geo-jeong's Viewpoint of Myeongli
sources.author: Kim Mantae
sources.repository: Korean Studies Institute / Korea Citation Index
sources.verified_scope: The accessible Korean and English abstracts identify Ohaengchonggwal as the earliest known Saju-Myeongri book written in Korea and Pirwonjapgi as the earliest Korean document using the term Saju, while emphasizing Seo Geo-jeong's Neo-Confucian framing and criticism of loose commercial claims.
sources.rights_note: Publisher copyright applies; the abstract is not a substitute for full-text or primary-source inspection.
sources.next_action: Locate surviving Ohaengchonggwal material and the precise Pirwonjapgi passages, verify their editions and determine whether any procedural content can be reconstructed.

sources.title: Saju
sources.repository: Encyclopedia of Korean Culture, Academy of Korean Studies
sources.verified_scope: The article defines four birth pillars, day-stem-centered synthesis, relations among stems and branches, six kinships, yin-yang and five-phase production/control, twelve life stages, spirit-stars, combinations and harms, major and annual fortune cycles, and includes worked chart tables. It maps contemporary Korean terminology and technique families but is not a controlling manual.
sources.rights_note: Academy of Korean Studies terms and article copyright apply.
sources.next_action: Recompute the worked chart and cycles independently, trace each technique to named Korean editions and determine which conventions are school-specific.

sources.title: Manyeonlyeok
sources.repository: Digital Jangseogak, Academy of Korean Studies
sources.verified_scope: The catalog describes a 1710-1776 royal Korean copy based on the Qing Shixian calendar, organized in twelve monthly volumes and used to predict month ends, new moons and solar terms; it later informed Joseon's Cheonse-ryeok production. The image-bearing record is a calendar witness, not a Saju interpretation manual.
sources.rights_note: Academy of Korean Studies states Some Rights Reserved; image reuse requires repository permission.
sources.next_action: Acquire representative images and a dated almanac series, transcribe solar-term and lunation entries, and reproduce them with a versioned historical calendar kernel.

sources.title: Yeoksamyeongwon
sources.author: Cao Zhen'gui; Joseon royal edition with preface
sources.repository: Digital Jangseogak, Academy of Korean Studies
sources.verified_scope: Jangseogak describes a five-volume work printed with a 1799 royal preface, probably used by Gwansanggam Myeonggwahak officials to judge daily auspiciousness and select dates. Its books cover stems/branches, month construction and year ruler, monthly auspicious and inauspicious spirits, mixed yin-yang doctrine and selection, with extensive named citations and author commentary.
sources.rights_note: Repository image terms apply; the work is Chinese-authored but the inspected witness and institutional use are Korean transmission evidence.
sources.next_action: Inspect all five image volumes, align headings and citations, and encode only an edition-specific Joseon electional pack after worked-date validation.

sources.title: Tojeong Bigyeol
sources.repository: Encyclopedia of Korean Culture, Academy of Korean Studies
sources.verified_scope: The article describes an annual Korean divination method using year ruler, month construction and day cycle, derives three figures from birth year/month/day without birth hour, uses forty-eight rather than sixty-four hexagrams, and gives twelve monthly verses. It also questions the attribution to Yi Ji-ham and places widespread seasonal use after the Jeongjo period.
sources.rights_note: Academy of Korean Studies article copyright applies.
sources.next_action: Establish the manuscript stemma and formula variants before selecting an edition; do not treat the traditional author attribution or one modern casting formula as settled.

sources.title: Tojeong Bigyeol
sources.author: Traditionally attributed to Yi Ji-ham
sources.repository: Digital Jangseogak, Academy of Korean Studies
sources.verified_scope: The item record identifies an undated, one-volume Classical Chinese witness, shelfmark PC9A-9A/C9A^9A, with 732 microfilm images available. The actual folios and formula variants were not inspected in this pass.
sources.rights_note: Academy of Korean Studies states Some Rights Reserved; image access and reuse terms apply.
sources.next_action: Acquire and inspect the full image set, record colophon and physical evidence, build a folio concordance, and compare its casting table and verses with other dated witnesses.

sources.title: Sinmi-year Saju Danja
sources.repository: Digital Jangseogak / Korean Historical Document Archive
sources.verified_scope: The one-sheet Classical Chinese marriage document records the groom's year, lunar month, day and double-hour sent to the bride's family. It is direct evidence for the social transmission of four birth components, not evidence for the matching judgment subsequently performed.
sources.rights_note: The image is supplied by Jeonbuk National University Museum and separately copyrighted; repository transcriptions and translations have their own terms.
sources.next_action: Collect paired marriage documents and any attached judgment or date-selection record, then reconstruct the exact calendar date and double-hour as a validation fixture.

sources.title: A Study on the Algorithmic Formalization of Saju-Myeongrihak Knowledge
sources.author: Chun Se-yun
sources.repository: Society of Eastern Culture and Convergence / KoreaScholar
sources.verified_scope: The accessible 2026 abstract classifies solar terms, five-element analysis and major-cycle calculation as fully formalizable; some spirit-star, twelve-stage, void and stem-combination rules as partially formalizable; and Yongshin selection as context-dependent expert judgment. It cites four Chinese classical works and reports experience with a calculation program, but the full article is paywalled and no implementation was inspected.
sources.rights_note: Publisher copyright and paywall apply; abstract-only access cannot support rule encoding.
sources.next_action: Acquire and critically review the full paper, reproduce its classifications against the cited passages, and test whether the claimed non-formalizability reflects source ambiguity, school variation or an avoidable underspecification.

sources.title: Problems of the Current Calendar System
sources.repository: Korea Astronomy and Space Science Institute
sources.verified_scope: The institutional PDF timed out during direct inspection, so no historical offset or daylight-saving datum from indexed snippets is accepted as evidence.
sources.rights_note: Unknown until the paper and publication metadata are retrieved.
sources.next_action: Acquire the KASI paper and legal enactments, then build authoritative Korean civil-time fixtures for every offset and daylight-saving transition before calculating an hour pillar.

sources.title: A Brief History of Vietnamese Astronomy and Calendars During the Reign of the Royal Dynasties
sources.author: Pham Vu Loc and Le Thanh Lan
sources.repository: Springer chapter; author-uploaded full text on ResearchGate
sources.verified_scope: The full chapter documents Vietnamese royal astronomy offices, named calendar regimes, regional and dynastic changes, surviving Bach Trung Kinh calendar runs, solar terms, lunations, intercalation, planets and hemerological responsibilities. It explicitly supports historical Vietnamese calendars as locally produced and sometimes divergent from Chinese calendars; it is a secondary source map rather than an atomic rule authority.
sources.rights_note: Springer copyright applies; the inspected author-uploaded text is for research use and must not be redistributed without permission.
sources.next_action: Acquire the cited Vietnamese manuscripts and dated almanacs, map every regime by dynasty and region, and validate reconstructed month and day labels against primary calendar pages.

sources.title: How to compute the Vietnamese lunar calendar
sources.verified_scope: The page states that a month begins on the Vietnamese civil day containing New Moon, month 11 contains the winter solstice, and in a thirteen-month span the first post-solstice month lacking a principal term is intercalary. It supplies GMT, Hanoi and Beijing event tables for 1984-1985 and demonstrates date and month-number divergence caused by local civil-day placement.
sources.rights_note: Site copyright and reuse terms were not established; use as calculation evidence and fixture lead, not redistributable content.
sources.next_action: Recompute every event with a named ephemeris, validate against two independent Vietnamese almanac series, and establish the supported civil-time and longitude-reference range before implementation.

sources.title: Old-time Luni-solar Calendars in Vietnam
sources.author: Kazuhiko Okazaki
sources.verified_scope: Repository search metadata identifies the paper and an approximately 934 KB PDF named 05_Okazaki.pdf, but the PDF could not be opened during this audit. No calendrical claim from snippets was promoted.
sources.rights_note: Repository and article terms remain to be inspected with the PDF.
sources.next_action: Acquire the PDF through the repository or interlibrary access, inspect its sources and tables, and compare its historical conversions with Vietnamese primary almanacs.

sources.title: Hai cha con ho Dang va lich hoc Viet Nam xua
sources.verified_scope: The indexed record is a potentially relevant study of Dang Nhu Lam, Dang Lo and historical Vietnamese calendrical learning, but robots access failed. Search-result descriptions are not accepted as evidence for dates, methods or accuracy claims.
sources.rights_note: Journal copyright and access terms remain to be established.
sources.next_action: Retrieve the article through VJOL or a library, verify its bibliography and primary citations, and add only passage-supported transmission claims.

sources.title: Tu vi
sources.author: Wikipedia contribution republished by VOER
sources.verified_scope: The page inventories twelve palaces, main and auxiliary star groups, birth inputs, general chart-construction order and several reported Vietnamese-Chinese or intra-Vietnamese variant points. It also says construction is comparatively rule-like while interpretation varies. Its legendary history, self-corrections and lack of passage-level editions prevent any listed procedure from serving as sole rule authority.
sources.rights_note: VOER states CC BY 3.0 unless an exception is noted; attribution and upstream Wikipedia revision provenance still require verification.
sources.next_action: Use its Vietnamese titles and disagreement list only to locate named editions and worked charts; adjudicate every construction and timing variant from primary or critically edited sources.

sources.title: Ziwei Doushu Quanshu
sources.verified_scope: The complete three-juan table of contents and substantial construction text in juan 2 were inspected. The transcription exposes life/body palaces, a leap-month instruction, twelve-palace order, five-phase bureau, principal and auxiliary star placements, Four Transformations, direction rules and timing material, but the page does not establish its base edition or collation accuracy.
sources.rights_note: The underlying Qing work is marked public domain; Wikisource transcription is CC BY-SA 4.0 with site terms.
sources.next_action: Identify and acquire a dated facsimile of the same lineage, collate the construction section character by character, and reproduce worked charts before promoting any table.

sources.title: Ziwei Doushu Quanshu, juan 2
sources.verified_scope: The inspected text gives explicit algorithms and tables for life/body palace placement from lunar month and double-hour, treating an intercalary month as the following month for that operation, reverse placement of twelve topics, five-phase bureau setup, many stars keyed by hour/month/day/year stem/year branch, and the ten-stem Four Transformations table.
sources.rights_note: The underlying work is public domain; Wikisource transcription and reuse are governed by CC BY-SA 4.0.
sources.next_action: Create passage IDs and a diplomatic collation against a facsimile; then encode construction independently from interpretation and validate all stems, bureaus, leap-month cases and double-hour boundaries.

sources.title: Ziwei Doushu in the Zhengtong Daozang
sources.verified_scope: The catalog maps a three-juan work titled Ziwei Doushu to Zhengtong Daozang facsimile volumes 1114-1115. It is retained as a separate Daoist-canon witness and is not presumed to be the later natal chart system.
sources.rights_note: Underlying historical text may be public domain; Chinese Text Project image and access terms apply.
sources.next_action: Inspect all facsimile pages and catalog metadata, identify date and textual lineage, and compare terminology with the later Quanshu only to document non-identity.

sources.title: Tablets from the Sippar Library XIII: Enuma Anu Ellil XX
sources.author: F. N. H. Al-Rawi and A. R. George
sources.verified_scope: The complete 35-page article and rendered representative pages were inspected. It publishes IM 124485, a Late Babylonian Sippar witness covering EAE 20 sections VII-XIII, and compares the manuscript with Middle Assyrian, Middle Babylonian, Neo-Assyrian, Neo-Babylonian, and Late Babylonian witnesses. The edition demonstrates that the tablet had no single uniform text: directions, dates, eclipse duration, clause boundaries, and apodoses vary, including peace versus plunder and destruction versus prosperity. Ten IM passage units and seventeen witness-scoped rules or recensional variants are encoded with eleven vectors shared with an independent 2021 Assur edition. All reject birth input and customer prediction.
sources.rights_note: The journal article and tablet photographs remain under their publisher, authors, and holding-institution terms. The project stores derived normalized facts and a checksum, not the PDF or images.

sources.title: The Upadesa Sutra of Jaimini (an old treatise on Astrology), critically edited with the editor's own Sanskrit commentary, exhaustive English introduction, English translation and appendices
sources.author: Jaimini; edited by Prof. K. V. Abhyankar
sources.edition: Gujarat Vidyasabha / Sheth B. J. Institute of Learning and Research, Ahmedabad, Research Series No. 36, first edition A.D. 1951 (V.S. 2007), 500 copies
sources.verified_scope: The controlling scholarly witness. Foreword and title page confirm: Adhyayas 1-2 critically edited from 15 manuscripts; Adhyayas 3-4 edited for the first time from 3 manuscripts; commentary supplied by the editor only through Adhyaya 3 Pada 3. The item's OCR recovered the full English apparatus (introduction paragraphs 1-130, the complete English translation of the sutras, and the contents of four appendices) but recovered ZERO Devanagari - the Sanskrit pages OCR'd to Latin gibberish. Sutras 1.1.1-1.1.35 were read in translation and aligned passage by passage against the Sutrarthaprakasika Sanskrit. Introduction paragraph 51 states the chara-karaka degree rule and the eight-karaka scheme with Rahu and Ketu counted as one; paragraphs 105-129 contain 14 worked Karaka-kundalis of named modern figures; Appendix 1 is the Jaimini-Sutra-Karika, Appendix 4 a comparative contents table against Brhad-Yavana-Jataka, Brhajjataka, Saravali and Brhat Parasari.
sources.rights_note: 1951 Indian publication; copyright status not resolved. The uploader applied CC BY-NC-ND 4.0, which an uploader cannot grant on another party's work. Used for internal alignment and research paraphrase only pending a jurisdictional rights decision. The underlying Sanskrit sutra text is far older and is quoted from the public-domain witness instead.
sources.next_action: Obtain the page images to recover the Devanagari that the OCR lost, then collate Abhyankar's critical text against the Sutrarthaprakasika and the Jammu Nilakantha manuscript. Inspect paragraphs 105-129 for the 14 worked charts and extract birth data and stated judgments as a worked-example suite.

sources.title: Jaiminiyasutram, sutrarthaprakasikopetam (with the Sutrarthaprakasika Sanskrit commentary)
sources.author: Jaimini; commentary attributed in the Archive record to Rama Ratna Ojha's line of Sutrartha Prakasika transmission - authorship not yet confirmed from the title page
sources.repository: Internet Archive / Digital Library of India item 2015.242319
sources.edition: Benares, printed by Jayabhushana Dasa and Company / Ram Das Brijnath Das, Kachauri Gali, Banaras City; DLI citation date 1951
sources.verified_scope: The primary Sanskrit witness for this pack and by far the best Devanagari OCR of the five retrieved objects (104,988 Devanagari characters, largely legible). Adhyaya 1 Pada 1 sutras 1-33 were read in the original with the commentary. The commentary is a genuine critical instrument: it names and argues against Nilakantha twice (on chandasa sandhi at 1.1.4 and on the Hora/Bhava Lagna starting point at 1.1.31), against the Subodhini author three times (argala target, karaka tie-break, sammukha method), and against Premanidhi Pandita once (the sense of bhuyasa at 1.1.5). It quotes vrddha karikas for rasi drsti, the chara-karaka degree ranking, the Rahu reverse-count convention, the Hora/Bhava Lagna rates and the Varnada construction, and quotes a Brhat-Parasara-Hora-Saramsa passage on the seven karakas. Its running sutra text has SEVEN chara karakas and no Pitrkaraka sutra, and it explicitly reports and rejects the manuscripts that do carry one.
sources.rights_note: Digital Library of India scan; the Archive metadata rights field is empty and no licence is asserted. The underlying Sanskrit sutra text is long out of copyright. Treated as usable for quotation of the original with the rendering and citation shown alongside, per the corpus translation policy.
sources.next_action: Confirm the commentator's name and date from the title page images, correct the OCR against the page images for every sutra quoted in extraction_notes.md, and continue the reading through Adhyaya 1 Padas 2-4.

sources.title: Jaimini Sutram, Sanskrit-Hindi-tika-sahitam 'Tattvadarsa'
sources.author: Jaimini; Hindi commentary by Sitarama Jha
sources.repository: Internet Archive (Kirtikant Sharma Najafgarh / New Delhi Collection, eGangotri, Sarayu Trust)
sources.edition: Benares, Master Khelari Lal and Sons, illustrated, undated
sources.verified_scope: Third witness, used for corroboration rather than rule extraction. 126,548 Devanagari characters; OCR readable in the Hindi prose, less reliable in the Sanskrit. The editor's Hindi preface is independently valuable: it states that the text is distinguished from other jataka works by sign and planetary drsti, results via the atmadi karakas, results from pada and upapada, chara/sthira dasa results, and ayurdaya reckoned by several methods - an inventory that matches this pack's divergence claim. It also names Nilakantha and Kesava among the older commentators and karika authors, independently corroborating the Nilakantha attribution. This edition appears to cover two adhyayas.
sources.rights_note: Uploader applied CC0. The underlying Sanskrit is out of copyright; Sitarama Jha's Hindi tika is treated as potentially in copyright and is used for corroboration only, not quoted at length.
sources.next_action: Establish the edition date from the title page. Collate its Sanskrit sutra text against the Sutrarthaprakasika to produce a three-witness apparatus for Adhyaya 1 Pada 1.

sources.title: Jaimini Sutra with Vyakhya of Neelkanth (MS 882 Gha, Almirah 5, Shelf 1, Devanagari, Jyotisha)
sources.author: Jaimini; commentary (vyakhya) of Nilakantha
sources.repository: Internet Archive / eGangotri, from the manuscripts of the Dharmartha Trust, Raghunath Temple, Jammu
sources.verified_scope: The only DIRECT witness to Nilakantha's commentary retrieved. Manuscript OCR quality is poor (28,648 Devanagari characters, much of it garbled, with running heads and marginalia interleaved). Content is identifiable: the visible folios discuss lagnesa and dasamesa in movable/fixed/dual pairings yielding dirgha, madhya and alpa ayus - the Jaimini three-fold longevity determination - and reference hora lagna. NO rule in this pack is extracted from this manuscript. Every Nilakantha position encoded in the manifest rests on the Sutrarthaprakasika's QUOTATION of him, which is stated as such on each rule.
sources.rights_note: CC0 as applied by the digitizing trust.
sources.next_action: This is the highest-value outstanding item. Commission Devanagari manuscript transcription of the folios covering Adhyaya 1 Pada 1 so that Nilakantha can be read directly instead of through a hostile quoter, and so his positive rule for the Hora/Bhava Lagna starting point can be recovered.

sources.title: GRETIL retrieval attempt for the Jaimini Upadesa Sutra
sources.verified_scope: The full GRETIL index (1,033,721 bytes, Last-Modified 2020-09-14) was downloaded and searched. GRETIL carries five Jaimini items - Jaimini-Grhyasutra, Jaimini Mimamsasutra, Mimamsasutra with commentary 1-7, Jaiminiya-Brahmana, Jaiminiya-Upanisad-Brahmana and Jaiminiyanyayamalavistara - and NONE is the astrological Upadesa Sutra. sources.title: 文殊師利菩薩及諸仙所說吉凶時日善惡宿曜經 (Xiuyao jing / Sukuyokyo), Taisho T21 no. 1299
sources.author: 不空 Amoghavajra, translator (759 CE); 楊景風 Yang Jingfeng, annotator (764 CE)
sources.repository: CBETA (Chinese Buddhist Electronic Text Association), TEI P5 corpus published on GitHub
sources.verified_scope: Both fascicles were retrieved on 2026-08-02, hash-pinned, and flattened to a line-addressed rendering keyed to Taisho page, column and line (1052 lines, sha256 efc2b8de7e6ecf2b93b153c5f5743b6732dfd917090d3842bc68cd50a48b6cdb). The Classical Chinese was read directly; no modern translation was used. Passages inspected and encoded include chapter 1 (the twelve 宮 with their pada allotments and resident luminaries, and the three lunar-conjunction classes), chapter 2 (the mansion figure catalogue with its day-election and natal clauses), chapter 3 三九祕宿品 (the three-nine relationship table, the bidirectional association test, the election categories and the planetary-affliction inversion), chapter 4 七曜直日品 (the seven weekday luminaries with their natal and mundane clauses), the fascicle-2 二十七宿十二宮圖 section (month naming by full-moon mansion, and both the primary and abbreviated birth-mansion procedures), the 二十七宿所為吉凶曆 almanac, 三必祕要法 (a second independent statement of the three-nine table with explicit ordinals, plus a printed worked example rooted on 畢), and chapter 8 七曜直日曆品 (the Sogdian/Persian/Sanskrit weekday-name table and the three weekday-mansion combination classes). Four independent statements in the text put the operative cycle at 二十七宿, and the pada arithmetic closes at 12 x 9 = 108 = 27 x 4 with zero pada allotted to 牛; the 28-fold list survives only in the chapter 2 figure catalogue, where the 牛 entry uniquely lacks a day-election clause. Internal contradictions were recorded rather than resolved, including opposite verdicts on the 業 day in chapter 3 and in 三必祕要法, a self-contradiction about marriage on a 危 day inside 三必祕要法, two non-mansion graphs in the 羅剎日 table, and a thirteen-mansion enumeration at T21.0387a20 that conflicts with the pada allotment printed nine lines later.
sources.rights_note: NOT public domain by assumption. The CBETA TEI header states: 'Available for non-commercial use when distributed with this header intact.' The stored XML retains that header unmodified. The underlying Taisho shinshu daizokyo edition carries its own publisher terms, which were not independently cleared in this pass. Research use inside the repository is within the stated condition; reproducing the transcription as customer-facing product content requires separate rights review.
sources.next_action: Collate the CBETA transcription against a second witness (SAT Daizokyo or a Taisho facsimile) at the passages where characters are doubtful; obtain an independent Classical Chinese reader and a Buddhist-astral-science specialist to check the passage-to-predicate encoding; and secure a named lunisolar calendar regime before any birth mansion is computed for a real date.

sources.title: 七曜攘災決 (Qiyao rangzai jue), Taisho T21 no. 1308
sources.author: 金俱吒, a brahmin monk of West India (西天竺國婆羅門僧)

sources.verified_scope: All three fascicles were retrieved on 2026-08-02, hash-pinned, and flattened to a 975-line rendering (sha256 50b9c1481eb25c8eefc97962602cb45f142039fcbe71a2a9df6983e627937a7d). Inspected structurally and at the opening: the text summons 二十八宿 deities, not twenty-seven; it defines 命宿 as the mansion where the Sun and Moon stand at the time of birth, which is a different definition from T1299's mansion of the lunar birth day; it carries a 宿度法 apportioning mansions in degrees by cardinal quadrant, in which 牛 receives an entry; it carries seven per-planet apotropaic chapters and a twelve-place scheme (命宮, 財宮, 兄弟, 田宅, 男女, 僮僕, 妻妾, 疾病, 遷移, 官位, 福相, 困窮) evaluated against the seven luminaries plus 羅睺 and 計都. NO rule was encoded from this text. Its tables are printed as grids in the Taisho and CBETA's linearization of them is unusable as data; the quadrant degree totals as transcribed (75, 98, 80, 113) sum to 366 rather than the 365.25 of a Chinese 周天, and that discrepancy was recorded rather than corrected. The text is registered as a contrast witness proving that T1299's 27-mansion system and this 28-mansion system must not be merged.

sources.next_action: Obtain a Taisho facsimile or a modern edition that preserves the table layout before any degree, ephemeris or twelve-place material is encoded; keep the 28-mansion scheme in a separate pack from T1299 under all circumstances.

Opening inspected: the text opens with 二十八宿在天左轉 and runs a nine-luminary (九曜) age cycle in which each luminary governs a set of years of life, with mantras and offering instructions per luminary. This is a third scheme, distinct from both T1299's 27-mansion cycle and T1308's 28-mansion degree apportionment. It is registered as a contrast witness only. NO rule was encoded from it, and it must not be used to supply mansion counts, birth mansions or delineations to the T1299 pack.

sources.title: NDL Search catalogue leads for the Japanese Sukuyodo reception layer
sources.verified_scope: Queried on 2026-08-02; twenty records returned and read as metadata only. None was opened and none is cited by any rule. The Sukuyodo pack therefore contains NO Japanese-side rule: everything encoded is from the Chinese Taisho text that the Japanese tradition read, and the Japanese reception layer is declared source_gated rather than assumed identical. The leads that would lift that gate are: Akazawa Haruhiko, 『院政期・鎌倉期の宿曜道と宿曜師』 (2021, NDL R100000136-I1010009142284836736), the standard modern study of the institution and its practitioners; Mizuguchi Motoki, 「陰陽道・宿曜道別立隆盛の淵源―〈術数文化〉の視点から」 (2021), which argues the separate establishment of Onmyodo and Sukuyodo and would let this repository rest its disambiguation on external authority rather than on its own reading; Shigeta Shinichi, 「陰陽師VS宿曜師 暦の利権をめぐる争い」 on the institutional rivalry over calendar authority; Udai Takafumi, 「円形式北斗曼荼羅考 : 高山寺蔵『宿曜占文抄』をめぐって」 (NDL R000000004-I023457152), which names the Kozan-ji 宿曜占文抄 manuscript, the highest-value Japanese-side target; and Jeffrey Kotyk, 「漢訳アビダルマにおける宇宙論と『宿曜経』」 (2021), by the working specialist on the Xiuyao jing's transmission and the natural independent reviewer for this pack.
sources.rights_note: Catalogue metadata only; no content was obtained or reproduced.
sources.next_action: Acquire an edited or digitized text of 『宿曜占文抄』 or a dated Sukuyodo kanmon from the Insei/Kamakura corpus, which is the single acquisition that would convert this track from 'the Chinese text the Japanese read' into 'what Japanese sukuyoshi actually did with it'.
